Hi,
I have the following data:

res=data.frame(fn=c('S1','S1','S2','S2','S3','S3'),
stype=c('N','N','N','N','P','P'),
eye=c('OS','OS','OD','OD','OS','OS'),
freq=c(30,60,30,60,30,60),
value=c(0.1,0.15,0.2,0.125,0.75,0.225))

which gives:

   fn stype eye freq value
1 S1     N  OS   30 0.100
2 S1     N  OS   60 0.150
3 S2     N  OD   30 0.200
4 S2     N  OD   60 0.125
5 S3     P  OS   30 0.750
6 S3     P  OS   60 0.225

and i need to reshape into:

   fn stype eye freq.30  freq.60
1 S1    N  OS  0.100    0.150
2 S2    N  OD  0.200    0.125
3 S3    P  OS  0.750   0.225

As of my understanding it should be possible with "cast", but i do not
get the syntax.

Any help appreciated.

Thanks,
Herbert

this should work:

res=data.frame(fn=c('S1','S1','S2','S2','S3','S3'),
stype=c('N','N','N','N','P','P'),
eye=c('OS','OS','OD','OD','OS','OS'),

value1=c(0.1,0.15,0.2,0.125,0.75,0.225),
value2=c(1.1,1.15,1.2,1.125,1.75,1.225))

library(reshape)

# using melt
resm <- melt(res, id.vars=1:4)
resc <- cast(fn+stype+eye ~ freq + variable, data=resm)
resc

> 2. Is there an option to drop or ignore columns (so no aggregation
> takes place)?

hmm, not sure if I understand you correctly. Maybe "subset" the data
at first or something like

res=data.frame(fn=c('S1','S1','S2','S2','S3','S3'),
stype=c('N','N','N','N','P','P'),

xtype=c('B','K','K','B','O','F'),

eye=c('OS','OS','OD','OD','OS','OS'),

value1=c(0.1,0.15,0.2,0.125,0.75,0.225),
value2=c(1.1,1.15,1.2,1.125,1.75,1.225))

# drop column "xtype"
resm <- melt(res, id.vars=c(1,2,4,5), measure.vars=c("value1",
"value2"))
resc <- cast(fn+stype+eye ~ freq + variable, data=resm)
resc

Patrick

messages.body_plain:
in your case, the xx is continuous variable.
so you can do that by either

ggplot(dd,aes(factor(xx),yy))+geom_bar(stat="identity")+scale_x_discrete(breaks=c(1,5,10),labels=c("a","b","c"))

or

ggplot(dd,aes(xx,yy))+geom_bar(stat="identity")+scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(1,5,10),labels=c("a","b","c"))

and probably ggplot2 list is more suitable for your question.

apply(mtcars,2,quantile, 0.75)
